text: When an AI agent spends money, who is accountable?
This is SettleAI. It makes sure the work was done before PayPal pays, and it says who is liable when it wasn't.
Ravi runs a small shop. His AI agent can hire couriers for him, but only within limits he signs: delivery jobs, up to a hundred and fifty dollars each.
Now the agent tries to book a five hundred dollar repair job. That's outside the limits. The check is plain code, not a prompt. It says no, and why, before any money moves.
Inside the limits, the agent books a delivery. Ravi pays through PayPal checkout, in the sandbox. PayPal holds the money for this job until the work is proven.
The courier sends a photo. Simple rules check the place, the time, and whether the photo was used before. Then an AI model checks each requirement, and the payment is approved.
On a second job, someone sends the same photo again. It's caught. Nothing is paid, and the job waits for a person in the review queue.

Back on the first job, Ravi says one carton arrived damaged. An AI arbiter weighs both sides and writes a liability finding. It cites the exact clause Ravi signed. Both sides accept, and PayPal pays out and refunds.
These are real PayPal sandbox transactions. The capture, the payout, and the refund, each with its own PayPal ID.
Every step is signed into a receipt. Anyone can check it in the browser, without trusting us. Change a single character, and the check fails, and shows what was changed.
AI agents are about to spend real money. SettleAI makes them accountable. Try it yourself at the link on screen.
